system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review:** The Seller’s “FINAL”, “agreed” and market-standard assertions are not buyer authority. No Amelia Frost written approval has been given for the cap or claims-period fallbacks. The Disclosure Letter also identifies unresolved facts inconsistent with several Seller Update assurances.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / **AUD 4.8m**. | 25% / **AUD 6m**; 20% only with prior written Amelia Frost authority identifying the draft. | **Reject; restore 25%.** Matching a conditional fallback does not authorise its use. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recovering only the excess. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Replace both thresholds and basket mechanics.** Seller’s proposal materially shifts smaller and aggregate losses to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | 18 months; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general warranties; 18 months only with Amelia’s written approval; category-specific periods elsewhere. | **Restore 24 months and delete the all-Claims extension.** Neither the fallback nor cross-category application is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate **100% cap**, **at least six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject general-regime treatment.** Ownership and capacity risks require distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from **all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an express overriding carve-out.** This protection is mandatory and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. | **Specific fair disclosure**; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Delete blanket deemed disclosure and require specific fair disclosure.** Mere document availability must not defeat warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable through records. | Delete blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusions; any permitted knowledge qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, never excusing title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as proposed.** It converts diligence access and constructive knowledge into a broad liability escape. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or conditions evidence is supplied. | Effective consent **and evidence all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Require substantive pre-Completion satisfaction, not delivery alone.** A customer representing approximately 30% of revenue cannot be addressed by endeavours alone. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion; no repayment or final discharge supplied. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; deferred release only with an irrevocable undertaking **and Amelia’s approval**. | **Reject the unsupported deferred-release proposal.** Buyer needs verified debt discharge and protection against continuing security. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses treated as Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Specific funds-flow provision for **AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs**, or documented Seller funding. | **Reconcile conditions and on-costs and expressly allocate funding.** Silent omission risks leaving Buyer with a Completion-triggered liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open without independent payment verification. | Broader indemnity for the identified IP ownership/transfer exposure, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-transfer cure; verify payment status and obtain effective transfer evidence. | **Broaden protection and pursue the cure without assuming payment or non-payment.** Neither the narrow indemnity nor the unverified ledger establishes secure IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Preserve logs, investigate access and scope, require updates and assess applicable obligations without assuming a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. | **Keep the issue open and require evidence-led investigation and reporting.** Preliminary uncertainty supports neither dismissal nor a concluded breach allegation. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate described as ordinary-course costs; disclosure leaves timing, scope, accrual, termination and avoidability unresolved. | Assess DD-008 and DD-011 together and establish the contractual and accounting facts. | **Investigate before agreeing treatment; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** Neither Seller’s ordinary-course assertion nor adverse price treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations presumptively extend across all Claims. | Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories, with explicit applicable regimes and no hidden general override. | **Delete global sweep-up wording and state category precedence expressly.** General warranty limits must not silently dilute distinct obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 internal share register said to evidence 100% ownership. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, beyond the supplied register. | **Require independent verification and supporting evidence.** DD-012 identifies the Seller’s source but is not independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties asserted to be settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms **open**, separately negotiated and expressly documented; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Reject the claimed settlement and reserve the substantive terms.** Seller’s assertion cannot establish Buyer agreement or determine the applicable liability regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
